newsitem.title: USA: AOL sees lawsuit as publicity stunt.
newsitem.headline: AOL sees lawsuit as publicity stunt.

text.p: America Online Inc said a lawsuit filed against it on Tuesday by Ben Ezra Weinstein and Co was without merit and said it appeared to be a publicity stunt by the small financial services firm.

Ben Ezra Weinstein had said it sued AOL in a New Mexico court seeking damages that could amount to several million dollars for what it claimed was AOL's failure to correct erroneous stock quotes carried on the online service.
"We can't see how this company was injured," said an AOL spokeswoman of the company's complaint. "When we learned about it we moved quickly to remedy the situation.
"This appears to have a lot more to do with a small company trying to get free publicity than with any real legal issue. We believe the suit is completely without merit."
The spokeswoman said AOL believed the problem originated with faulty data provided by its stock quotation supplier, Standard & Poors, a unit of McGraw-Hill Cos Inc.

A spokesman for McGraw-Hill said the company declined to comment until it had more details about the suit. The complaint against AOL, a copy of which was delivered to Reuters, made no mention of Standard & Poors.
Ben Ezra Weisman is an Albuquerque, N.M.-based firm that assists companies in filing public or private offerings.
